chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Mufazzal, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and a man asked him regarding how much Zakat is obligated from the wealth. He said to him: 'Do you intend the apparent Zakat or the hidden Zakat?' He said, 'I intend both of them together.' He said: 'As for the apparent, it is twenty-five in every thousand, and as for the hidden, do not monopolize for yourself what your brother is more in need of than you are.'

key_terms.خَمْسَةٌ وَ عِشْرُونَ: Twenty-five (referring to the rate of 2.5% or 25 per 1000)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between apparent and hidden Zakat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the juridical obligation of Zakat (2.5%) and its spiritual essence, defining the 'hidden' Zakat as the voluntary generosity shown to those in greater need. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the interplay between fixed legal duties (Fard) and the moral imperative of selflessness (Ihsan), where true wealth purification extends beyond mere calculation to include empathetic distribution.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al Mufazzal who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, and a man asked himasws, ‘With regards to how much is the Zakāt Obligated from the wealth?’ So heasws said to him: ‘Is it the apparent Zakāt or the hidden Zakāt are you intending?’ So he said, ‘I intend both of them together’. So heasws said: ‘As for the apparent, so it is twenty-five in every thousand, and as for the hidden, so not (considering as too much) preferring your brother with what he is more needy to it than you are’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from those whom he has mentioned (in his book) from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal who has said the following:

“Once I was in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, when a man asked him, ‘For how much property is it compulsory to pay zakat?’ The Imam asked him, ‘Do you mean thereby the apparent or unapparent zakat?’ He replied, ‘I mean both kinds.’ The Imam said, ‘The apparent kind is twenty-five due upon every one thousand. The unapparent kind is what you should not spare from your brother what he needs more than you do.’”
